title: Gabriel answers: do not fear, grace is above nature

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 11, cols. B-C (PDF p. 35)

source_text: Haec dum intra se cogitaret sanctissima Virgo, talibus Archangelus sermonibus disceptationem eius solvit, dicens ad ipsam: Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi. Ideo et quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei. Et ne timeas Maria: non enim ut metum tibi incuterem, adveni; sed ut metus materiam a te repellerem. Ne timeas Maria: invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum. Ne diiudices gratiam secundum naturam. Legibus enim naturae, se subiici gratia non patitur.
pass_a_gloss: These things while within herself she was pondering (cogitaret), the most holy Virgin, with such words (sermones) the Archangel resolved (solvit) her questioning/debate (disceptatio), saying to her: The Holy Spirit will come upon (superveniet) you, and the power of the Most High (virtus Altissimi) will overshadow (obumbrabit) you. Therefore also what will be born (nascetur) of you holy (sanctum) will be called (vocabitur) Son of God (Filius Dei). And do not fear (ne timeas), Mary: for not that I might strike fear (metum incuterem) into you did I come; but that I might drive away (repellerem) from you the matter/cause of fear (metus materia). Do not fear, Mary: for you have found grace (gratia) with God. Do not judge (diiudices) grace according to nature (secundum naturam). For to the laws of nature (leges naturae) grace does not suffer (non patitur) itself to be subjected (subiici).

choices.choice: The first 'Et ne timeas Maria' opens the author's own expansion and is left uncited; the full clause 'Ne timeas Maria: invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum' carries the citation.
Margin variant 'al. legi' (singular 'law') not adopted; it does not change the sense.

pass_b_english: While the most holy Virgin was thinking these things over within herself, the Archangel settled her questioning with words like these, saying to her: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy one who will be born of you will also be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). And do not fear, Mary: for I have not come to strike fear into you, but to drive the cause of fear away from you. Do not fear, Mary; for you have found grace with God (Luke 1:30). Do not judge grace by the measure of nature; for grace does not allow itself to be made subject to the laws of nature.
notes: Margin 'Ib. Luc. 1': Luke 1:35 and Luke 1:30. Section 1 renders 'gratiam apud Deum' as 'favor with God'; here 'grace with God' is used because the next two sentences play on gratia ('do not judge grace by nature'), and 'favor' would break the link. The first 'Et ne timeas Maria' opens the author's own expansion and is left uncited; the full clause 'Ne timeas Maria: invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum' carries the citation. Margin variant 'al. legi' (singular 'law') not adopted; it does not change the sense.
source_notes: PDF p. 35 = printed p. 11, cols. B-C; margin 'Ib. Luc. 1' (Luke 1:35, 1:30). Margin at 'Legibus': 'al. legi'.
